title: Shah Rukh Khan Takes Back Christmas — and Brings Suhana With Him. 'King' Locks December 25.
excerpt: SRK plays a lethal assassin, his daughter plays his protégé, and a 45-day gap from 'Ramayana' clears the runway for the comeback the diaspora has been waiting three years for.
body:
The cryptic posts have stopped. The date is real. Shah Rukh Khan is taking back Christmas, and he is bringing his daughter with him.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=M3mfut2RdHk

After weeks of director Siddharth Anand teasing fans with "announcement on the way" riddles on social media, the makers of King have locked December 25, 2026 for a global theatrical release — reclaiming the festive corridor Khan has owned for the better part of three decades. This is the slot that gave us the swoon of Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge and the spectacle of so many year-end blockbusters since. SRK in a Santa-season release isn't a date on a calendar. It's a homecoming.

!Shah Rukh Khan — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

**"I mentioned it to Sujoy one day and he says, 'Sir, I have a subject.'" — Shah Rukh Khan, at the Locarno Film Festival

And what a subject."**

"For 6-7 years I have been thinking about it. I mentioned it to Sujoy one day and he says, 'Sir, I have a subject.'" — Shah Rukh Khan, at the Locarno Film Festival

And what a subject. King is reportedly inspired by Luc Besson's 1994 cult classic Léon: The Professional — SRK as a sleek, lethal assassin, and Suhana Khan, in her full-fledged theatrical debut, as the protégé he can't quite keep at arm's length. After The Archies let her test the waters on Netflix, this is the deep end: a 350-crore action spectacle, her father opposite her, the entire industry watching to see if the Khan charisma is hereditary. (Early word from those who've seen the footage suggests it very much is.)

The casting sheet alone reads like a Filmfare cover shoot that refused to end. Abhishek Bachchan as the antagonist. Deepika Padukone, reuniting with the Pathaan universe's leading man. Anil Kapoor, Jackie Shroff, Arshad Warsi, and — in a piece of casting that made the internet briefly lose its composure — Rani Mukerji, sharing screen space with SRK again after all these years. There's even a whispered Ranveer Singh cameo. This is not an ensemble. It's a guest list.

!Locarno Film Festival — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The Christmas lock was no accident. Trade sources say the team eyed an earlier December 4 window but blinked, choosing to step well clear of Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, the most expensive Indian film ever mounted, with Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Yash as Ravana arriving for Diwali. By settling on December 25, the King camp engineered a clean 45-day gap — enough room for a divine epic and a modern action thriller to each breathe and bank without cannibalising one another. Smart. Khan's films have always understood the economics of the long weekend better than the analysts who cover them.

What makes this irresistible for the diaspora is timing and texture. A Christmas release is built for the overseas market — the NRI Friday-to-Sunday ritual of packed multiplexes in Edison, Hounslow, and Brampton, the WhatsApp groups lighting up with first-day-first-show plans. SRK's overseas pull is its own weather system; Pathaan became the first Hindi film to cross ₹500 crore, and a chunk of that thunder came from precisely these audiences. A December 25 date means the film lands right when families are home, the kids are out of school, and a three-hour SRK action drama is exactly the kind of event that fills a theatre.

The competition, to be fair, is ferocious. The same global Christmas corridor is jammed with Hollywood titans — Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday and Warner Bros' Dune 3 dropping a week prior on December 18, and Dwayne Johnson's Jumanji: Open World opening the very same day. SRK has never been shy about a fight on the international stage, but this is a heavyweight bracket. The question isn't whether King opens big at home — it will. It's whether Khan can hold his own against the Marvel machine on a Friday in London and New York.

The film has been shot across Mumbai, Warsaw, Gdansk, and Cape Town, with Anirudh Ravichander composing the score and Sachin–Jigar handling the songs — a soundscape engineered for maximum goosebumps. Anand, who turned Khan into a leaner, deadlier screen presence in Pathaan, is reportedly building "never-seen-before action blocks" here. If the teaser does what teasers for SRK comebacks tend to do, expect the view counts to be obscene by sunrise.

For now, the only number that matters is the one on the calendar. December 25. The King is coming home for the holidays, and he's brought an heir. After three years away from the big screen, that's the kind of return that doesn't need a trailer to sell it — though, knowing this team, the trailer will still break the internet.
